title: SysinternalsSuite staged on scranton ahead of LSASS access
rationale: Download and extraction of SysinternalsSuite (containing procdump) immediately preceding the lsass access; no dump utility command line observed, so generic OS Credential Dumping.

title: Steganographic PowerShell stager opens LSASS with full access on scranton
rationale: All describe the same action: hidden PowerShell PID 2976 (parent control.exe, decoding monkey.png) opened lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff at 03:05:16Z on scranton, plus the wsmprovhost LSASS handle on nashua. LSASS memory access is best fit by T1003.001.

title: SAM hive opened with 0xf003f by lsass.exe after attacker tooling
rationale: Five 4656 events show SAM opened with 0xf003f by lsass.exe right after attacker LSASS access and cleanup; Security Account Manager.

title: Clipboard harvesting via Get-Clipboard in pbeesly session
rationale: Get-Clipboard executed in the compromised session to harvest copied secrets; input capture, no keylogger code found.

title: Masqueraded .scr dropper and hidden steganographic PowerShell stager
rationale: ProgramData screen-saver dropper wrote monkey.png and control.exe launched the hidden stager that drove the credential-theft chain; input capture grouping.

title: PowerShell-driven csc.exe compiled attacker DLLs in Temp
rationale: csc.exe invoked by attacker PowerShell to compile DLLs in user Temp; grouped under input capture as the credential-access-adjacent action.

title: cmd.exe from .scr dropper launched attacker PowerShell chain
rationale: cmd.exe spawned by the .scr dropper launched the PowerShell chain performing credential theft.

title: Credential-harvesting toolkit: accesschk passwordsDB, discovery, archive staging
rationale: accesschk.exe wrote passwordsDB and cleartext pbeesly credentials were reused in PsExec64; credentials in files is the best fit for the collected credential artifacts.

title: Nashua: PsExec-launched python.exe ran credential-file harvesting and RAR staging
rationale: PowerShell collected *pass*/*login*/*admin* files into working.zip and password-protected it; credentials in files.

title: Registry reads of LSA and Winlogon keys by powershell.exe
rationale: 4663 events show powershell.exe reading LSA and Winlogon registry keys in the attacker session; credentials in registry.

title: sdclt.exe spawned by cmd.exe in attacker session
rationale: sdclt.exe started by cmd.exe just before the csc.exe compile; no credential access by sdclt observed, low confidence registry-credential context.

title: Private-key/certificate export and credential-store theft on scranton
rationale: Get-PrivateKeys exported every LocalMachine certificate private key to a password-protected .pfx, followed by LSASS access and cleanup; private key theft is the best fit.

title: User credential-bearing files archived and staged for exfiltration
rationale: Draft.Zip written and Downloads compressed into OfficeSupplies.7z then deleted; browser credential store theft is the closest in-scope fit for the user credential-file collection.

title: No Credential Manager/Vault access; LSASS handle is the only store-relevant hit
rationale: Finding explicitly reports no Credential Manager activity; the only credential-store-relevant event is the LSASS handle, assessed under Windows Credential Manager as the closest in-scope store technique.

title: Adversary-in-the-middle positioning confirmed by L2 redirection
rationale: L2 redirection and self-signed cert notices establish AiTM; ARP/ROUTE/ipconfig hits attributed to Azure guest agent are benign.

title: SMB session to NASHUA relayed through rogue MAC with SAMR/LSAR enumeration
rationale: SMB 445 flows to 10.0.1.6 delivered via the rogue MAC with DCE-RPC SAMR/LSAR enumeration; name resolution poisoning and SMB relay.

title: ARP cache poisoning: single MAC fronts all off-subnet destinations
rationale: One MAC (12:34:56:78:9a:bc) is L2 responder for three different subnets, the signature of ARP cache poisoning.

title: WebDAV cookie set during exfiltration staging; no browser cookie theft
rationale: Only cookie activity is davclnt.dll DavSetCookie for WebDAV exfil; no browser cookie theft or forgery observed.
